info.description: This is the API documentation for the backend service
info.title: Backend API

get.description: Returns all cleanup policies

post.description: Creates a new cleanup policy and reloads the scheduler. condition is a comma-separated list of key:value pairs (all must match): status:<status>; idle_days:<N> (no deploy for N days, creation time when never deployed; a running or partial instance whose expiry is in the future never matches); age_days:<N> (created more than N days ago); stopped_days:<N> (stopped, and the last stop finished N or more days ago; instances without a recorded stop time never match); cleaned_days:<N> (a draft, and the last clean finished N or more days ago; instances without a recorded clean time never match); ttl_expired; expires_within_hours:<N> (no expiry, or the expiry is at most N hours from now; an instance with a later expiry does not match).

put.description: Updates an existing cleanup policy and reloads the scheduler. Partial update: only the fields in the body change (for example {"enabled": false}); the merged policy is validated. See the create endpoint for the condition syntax (status, idle_days, age_days, stopped_days, cleaned_days, ttl_expired, expires_within_hours).

delete.description: Deletes a cleanup policy and reloads the scheduler

post.description: Executes a cleanup policy immediately and answers when the run ends. Use ?dry_run=true to preview matches without acting. Stop and clean only start the operations (fast). A delete runs the pre-instance-delete hooks per instance first, so a delete run can take up to the number of matches times (5 minutes, or the sum of the pre-instance-delete hook timeouts plus one minute when longer); use a client timeout that allows this. The run fires cleanup-policy-executed when at least one instance matched.

get.description: Returns all notification channels with subscription counts

post.description: Creates a new notification channel. A secret needs KUBECONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY: without the key a non-empty secret gives 400. With the key the secret and the webhook URL are encrypted at rest; without the key the URL is stored in plaintext. The webhook URL is at most 2048 characters. format sets the body of the webhook request: "generic" (default, the event JSON) or "teams" (a Microsoft Teams Adaptive Card envelope for a Teams workflow made from the template "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received"). An unknown format gives 400. Optional filters limit the channel to some stack instances: instance_name_patterns (globs, path.Match syntax, case-insensitive), owner_ids, definition_ids and cluster_ids. Each set filter must match (AND); one value of a filter is enough (OR); empty filters match all instances. Events without an instance go only to channels without filters; a cleanup policy run goes to a channel when at least one affected instance matches. An invalid pattern gives 400. An ID that does not exist gives a warning in the response; the channel is saved.

get.description: Returns all known event types that channels can subscribe to
Returns a notification channel by ID, with its filters

put.description: Updates an existing notification channel. Only the fields in the body change. A new non-empty secret needs KUBECONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY (400 without it); "secret": "" removes the secret. A secret_unreadable or webhook_url_unreadable channel (stored value that cannot be decrypted) sends nothing until a PUT sets the value again. format ("generic" or "teams") replaces the body format; omit it to keep the format; an unknown format gives 400. filters replaces the channel filters (omit it to keep them, send {} to remove them); the rules are the same as for create. An ID that does not exist gives a warning in the response.

delete.description: Deletes a notification channel and its subscriptions

put.description: Replaces all event type subscriptions for a channel

post.description: Sends a test payload (event type "test") to the channel's webhook URL with one attempt, in the format of the channel (generic event JSON or a Teams Adaptive Card envelope). Redirects are not followed. A disabled channel can be tested too; channel_enabled in the response tells whether the channel gets events. Each test send is written to the delivery log of the channel with event_type "test".

200.description: success (bool), message, status_code (0 when no answer), channel_enabled (bool)

post.description: Authenticate with username and password, returns a JWT access token and sets a refresh token cookie. Without the correct password the answer is always 401 "Invalid username or password". A disabled account (403) or the SSO-only restriction (403) is shown only after a correct password.

Ends the sessions that the request proves: the session of the refresh token cookie and the session of a valid bearer token (its sid claim), also when the cookie is missing. When both name different sessions, both end. It revokes all refresh tokens of each session, then blocks the session in the session store, so that every access token of it (not only the presented one) gets 401, and its WebSockets close within the revalidation interval. It also blocklists the presented access token and closes its WebSockets. Access tokens of other sessions of the user keep working. A request without a cookie and without a valid bearer token ends nothing and answers 200. When the refresh token lookup or a revoke fails, the cookie is still cleared and the blocks are still written, but the answer is 500.

Revokes all refresh tokens for the current user, then blocks every session of the user that has a refresh token row whose expiry is later than now minus (access token lifetime + 1 minute + reuse grace), also when that refresh token was revoked earlier. A session block is a plain block, so every access token of those sessions is rejected, and cannot open a WebSocket, while the replica clocks differ by less than the 1 minute block margin. It also writes a user block that rejects every access token issued up to now. The refresh-token cleanup keeps rows for that window after they expire. A session without such a row (a login whose refresh token could not be stored) and a token without a session (the SSO CLI token) rely on the user block, which holds on replicas with synchronised (NTP) clocks. A login after the logout works. The presented access token is blocklisted and all WebSockets of the user close. When the revoke fails, the sessions get the long block (until the maximum session lifetime), the other blocks are still written, the cookie is cleared and the answer is 500. When only the listing of the sessions fails, the revoke and the user block still run and the answer is 200. When the listing and the revoke both fail, only the presented session is blocked and the answer is 500.

get.description: Handles the IdP callback after user authentication. Exchanges the authorization code for tokens, provisions or updates the local user, and redirects to the frontend with a JWT.

post.description: Generates a session ID and OIDC authorization URL for CLI-based SSO login. The CLI opens the returned login_url in a browser and polls cli-token until authentication completes. Optionally accepts a loopback `redirect_uri` (http scheme, any loopback IP such as 127.0.0.1 or [::1], or hostname "localhost", with an explicit port) for the RFC 8252 native-app flow — the callback then 302-redirects the browser directly to that URL with tokens in the query string, no polling needed.
Returns the current status of a CLI auth session. Returns pending while waiting for the user to complete browser authentication, or completed with a JWT token once done.

get.description: Returns public OIDC configuration for the frontend (enabled status, provider name, local auth availability)

post.description: Issues a new access token using the refresh token cookie. Rotates the refresh token (old one invalidated, new one issued). A session ends SESSION_MAX_LIFETIME after login and after SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT without requests; rotation never extends the session. A token rotated less than REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE ago (for example a concurrent refresh from a second browser tab) gets a new access token without a new cookie. Any other reuse of a consumed token revokes the session.

401.description: Invalid, expired, or revoked refresh token or session

Returns node count, CPU/memory totals, and namespace count for a cluster. requested_cpu and requested_memory are the sums of the pod requests of scheduled, unfinished pods (not real use); omitted when the pod list fails.
Returns all stack-* namespaces in the cluster.
Returns the resource quota configuration for a cluster, or 404 if not set.
get.summary: Get resource quota config for a cluster

put.description: Creates or updates the resource quota configuration for a cluster. Admin only. Each non-empty quantity must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (for example 500m, 2, 512Mi, 10Gi) and not negative; cpu_request must not exceed cpu_limit and memory_request must not exceed memory_limit; pod_limit must not be negative. The container_* fields set the LimitRange of each stack namespace (defaultRequest, default, max per container); per container, request <= limit <= max, and a container default must not exceed the namespace value of the same resource. ephemeral_storage_limit sets requests.ephemeral-storage and limits.ephemeral-storage of the namespace ResourceQuota. Without container defaults, the LimitRange uses fallback defaults (CPU 100m request / 500m limit, memory 128Mi / 512Mi, ephemeral storage 128Mi / 1Gi), capped at the namespace value and the container max; never the namespace total. Values are trimmed. Invalid input returns 400 with the field name. The quota is also checked merged with the quota override of every instance on the cluster (for the default cluster also instances without a cluster); a conflict returns 400 listing up to 10 instance names and the first rule broken. After the save, the backend applies the quota to every stack namespace on the cluster in the background: the namespace of an instance with a quota override gets the effective quota (the cluster quota merged with the override); other stack namespaces get the cluster quota. A namespace whose merged quota is not valid is skipped.

post.description:
Import a stack definition from a portable JSON bundle, creating a new definition with fresh IDs. Definition names are unique per owner: when the caller already has a definition with the bundle name, the import uses "<name> (imported)", then "<name> (imported 2)", ... The response holds the final name (409 when no free name is found).
definition.source_template (optional: id or name, and version) links the new definition to a template, as PUT /stack-definitions/{id}/template-link does. The import looks up the template by ID, else by name among the published templates (not case-sensitive on MySQL). When the template does not exist, is not published, the name matches more than one published template, or the version is not a published version, the import creates the definition without a link and adds a message to warnings; it does not fail.

get.description:
Check if the latest published snapshot of the source template has another version than the definition's current version. An unpublished template, or one without a snapshot, gives upgrade_available=false.
chart_diffs has the shape of the version diff chart_diffs: left = the definition charts now (locked values from the current source version snapshot), right = the charts as the upgrade writes them (default values, repository URL, deploy order, and chart version, chart path, source repository and build pipeline when the snapshot has them), with the locked values and required flags of the latest snapshot. change_type "removed" means the chart is only in the definition; the upgrade keeps it. changes lists the same charts by change_type, so both always agree.
Without an upgrade, reason says why: no_source_template (the definition has no source template), no_published_version (the template is not published or has no snapshot) or up_to_date (current_version is the latest_version).
get.summary: Check if a template upgrade is available

get.description: Export a stack definition and its chart configs as a portable JSON bundle

put.description:
Sets or removes the source template of an existing definition (for example an imported one). The link changes only source_template_id and source_template_version; the charts and the values of the definition do not change.
A linked definition gets the template rules: required charts cannot be removed, the locked values of the latest published snapshot apply at deploy time (also when the link names an older version; the version is the base of the upgrade check), the upgrade check compares with the template, and the analytics template usage counts the definition, its instances and its deploys. A definition whose charts differ from the template can be linked; the upgrade check then shows the difference.
template_id empty removes the link (both fields become empty; version must then be empty). The template must exist (404) and be published (409). version must be a published version of the template (400); empty means the latest published version.
Authorization: devops or admin (403).
put.summary: Link a stack definition to a template

post.description:
Upgrade a definition to the latest published snapshot of its source template, adding new charts and updating defaults, repository URL, deploy order and (when the snapshot has them) chart version, chart path, source repo and build pipeline. Charts that are only in the definition stay.
An unpublished template, or one without a snapshot, gives 409 "Template has no published version".
post.summary: Apply a template upgrade to a definition

The filters name, status, cluster_id, definition_id and owner combine (AND). total is the number of instances that match the filters.
owner is "me" (the authenticated user), a username, or a user ID. A value in UUID form is matched as a user ID first, then as a username. An unknown username or ID gives an empty list.
The list is paged (default pageSize 25); with owner=me or name the total is the real number of matches, not the page size.
Each instance includes owner_username, definition_name and cluster_name. A field is omitted when the owner, definition or cluster no longer exists; cluster_name is also omitted when cluster_id is empty (older instances).

Create a new stack instance from a definition.
The owner and the subscribed notification channels get the notification instance.created, with the caller as the trigger.
Expiry: ttl_minutes counts from the deploy (omitted: DEFAULT_INSTANCE_TTL_MINUTES; 0: no expiry). expires_at (RFC 3339 with a time zone) is a fixed stop time instead: ttl_minutes becomes 0, and a deploy keeps the stop time. expires_at must be in the future and not later than now + MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS (default 30). A TTL above that limit, or expires_at together with ttl_minutes, gives 400.

post.description: Clean multiple stack instances in a single request. Uninstalls Helm releases and deletes namespaces.

Delete multiple stack instances in a single request. Processes instances sequentially with the rules of DELETE /stack-instances/{id}: an instance with cluster resources (running, partial, stopped, error) is cleaned first (Helm uninstall and namespace delete) and deleted when the clean completes — its result has status "success" and the log_id of the clean. "success" with a log_id means that the clean started; the row is removed when the clean finishes (WebSocket message instance.deleted). A failed clean keeps the instance with status error. A draft instance is deleted at once. An instance with an operation in progress (checked before pre-instance-delete fires), one that a concurrent delete already started, or one that a pre-instance-delete hook rejects, gets status "error".
Deploy multiple stack instances in a single request. Processes instances sequentially.
Stop multiple stack instances in a single request. Processes instances sequentially.

get.description: Compare the merged values of two stack instances side-by-side, per chart. The merged values use the deploy pipeline: cluster shared values, chart defaults, value overrides, locked template values and chart branch overrides. charts[].has_differences is true when the merged YAML differs or the chart exists on one side only.
Returns the 5 most recently updated stack instances owned by the current user
get.summary: Get recent stack instances for the authenticated user

get.description: Get a stack instance by ID. values_drift is true when the running values come from a successful rollback and the stored overrides produce different values: the next deploy undoes the rollback. Only this endpoint computes values_drift, following (the caller follows the instance) and follower_count; list responses omit them. owner_username, definition_name and cluster_name are omitted when the owner, definition or cluster no longer exists; cluster_name is also omitted when cluster_id is empty (older instances).

put.description:
Update a stack instance (branch, name, etc.). A changed name must be a DNS label (lowercase a-z, 0-9, '-', start and end alphanumeric, at most 50 characters); an unchanged name is not checked, so older instances with other names stay editable. A rename does not change the namespace.
ttl_minutes sets a new TTL from now (0 clears the expiry). expires_at (RFC 3339 with a time zone) sets a fixed stop time and ttl_minutes 0. Do not send both (400). The limits are the same as for create (MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS).

200.description: The updated instance with the same computed fields as GET (values_drift, names, follow state)

403.description: Caller is not the owner, an admin or a devops user

409.description: The new name is taken on the cluster (UNIQUE_INSTANCE_NAMES)

delete.description: Deletes a stack instance. If the instance has running resources (status running/stopped/error), a cleanup is initiated first — helm releases are uninstalled and the namespace is deleted before the database record is removed. Returns 204 for immediate deletion (draft instances) or 202 when async cleanup is required: the clean started, and the row is removed when the clean finishes (WebSocket message instance.deleted). A failed clean keeps the instance with status error ("Clean failed; the stack was not deleted."). An operation in progress gives 409 before pre-instance-delete fires; of two concurrent deletes one gets 409. When quick deploy created the stack definition of the instance (owner_instance_id) and no other instance uses it, the definition and its charts are deleted with the instance.

202.description: Cleanup initiated, instance will be deleted after resources are removed

204.description: No Content — instance deleted immediately (no resources to clean)

403.description: Caller is not the owner, an admin or a devops user, or a pre-instance-delete hook rejected the request

409.description: Instance is in a transient state (deploying/stopping/cleaning), or a concurrent delete started first

503.description: Deploy manager not configured, or a pre-instance-delete hook could not check where it applies (applies_to)

get.description: Returns the stored custom action runs of the instance, newest first, with cursor paging (no total). Any authenticated user who can view the instance gets the list (the rule of the action list). parameters holds the declared parameters only; a sensitive parameter shows [redacted]. status_code 0 means that no answer came (the subscriber was unreachable, or the client closed the request). message is the refusal reason of the subscriber (a sensitive value sent with the call shows [redacted]) or a fixed text. started_by is omitted when the user no longer exists. action_label is the current label of the action, else its name. has_job_log is true when the run has a job_id and the action still has a log_path. can_view_logs is true for the owner, an admin and a devops user: only they may read a job log. Without a repository the list is empty.
get.summary: List the action runs of a stack instance

parameters.description: Rows per page (default 20; a value above 100 counts as 100)
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from next_cursor of the previous page
parameters.name: cursor

get.description: Returns the registered actions that apply to the instance (the applies_to of each action: templates, template categories, definitions, clusters) with their UI metadata (label, description, confirmation text, parameter schema) and a can_invoke flag. Any authenticated user who can view the instance gets the list; can_invoke is true for the owner, an admin and a devops user. When the template of the instance cannot be read, the actions limited to templates are left out and scope_incomplete is true. The response never contains the subscriber URL, secret, headers or applies_to. Without an action registry the list is empty.
get.summary: List the actions that can run on a stack instance

post.description: Dispatches to the action subscriber webhook and wraps its response in an envelope containing action, instance_id, status_code, and result fields. The subscriber's JSON body is nested under the result key. Returns 200 even for non-2xx subscriber responses — check status_code to distinguish. For an answer with status 400 or higher the envelope also has message: the subscriber's reason from a JSON string body or from the message, error, detail or reason field (one line, at most 500 characters, URLs replaced by [url]). A text/plain body of such an answer becomes a JSON string result; another non-JSON body gives a null result. A non-JSON body with a status below 400 gives 502. When the action declares parameters, they are checked (type, required, enum options) before the call; undeclared parameters pass through. When the action has a log_path, the subscriber answered 2xx and the result has a valid job_id, the envelope also has job_id: poll GET /stack-instances/{id}/actions/{name}/jobs/{job_id}/log for the job log. Each call that reaches the subscriber (also an unreachable subscriber or a non-JSON body) stores one action run (GET /stack-instances/{id}/action-runs) with the caller, the declared parameters only (a sensitive parameter as [redacted]), the status code, the message and the job_id. The envelope has run_id when the run was stored; a failed write never fails the call.
post.summary: Invoke a registered action against a stack instance

parameters.description: Optional parameters passed through to the subscriber
parameters.name: request

403.description: Caller is not the owner, an admin or a devops user

404.description: Instance not found, or action not registered or not for this instance (applies_to)

get.description: Fetches the job log of an asynchronous action from the action subscriber, from the byte offset to the end (at most 256 KiB per call). The action config must have a log_path. Poll with next_offset until done is true. The first poll that returns done stores the final job status and the finish time on the action run of the job (GET /stack-instances/{id}/action-runs); later polls change nothing. Only the instance owner, an admin or a devops user may read the job log (the same rule as invoke). The backend signs the subscriber request like an invoke call and never returns the subscriber URL.
get.summary: Read the job log of an asynchronous action

parameters.description: Job ID (1-128 characters: A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, not starting with a dot)
parameters.name: job_id

post.description:
Create a new draft stack instance as a copy of an existing one. The clone belongs to the caller and uses the cluster and definition of the source.
It copies the TTL (unless ttl_minutes or expires_at is given; a future fixed stop time of the source is copied too), the value overrides and the branch overrides. It copies the instance quota override only when the caller owns the source or is admin or devops; for an owner without the admin or devops role only when the override stays within the cluster quota. When it is not copied for that reason (or the cluster quota lookup fails), the response has a warning and the clone uses the cluster quota.
The body is optional. Without a name, the server picks the first free name of <source>-copy, <source>-copy-2, ... (the namespace stack-<name>-<owner> must be free). A given name must be a DNS label (lowercase a-z, 0-9, '-', start and end alphanumeric, at most 50 characters).
The owner and the subscribed notification channels get the notification instance.created, with the caller as the trigger.

parameters.description: Optional clone name, branch and TTL
parameters.name: body

409.description: Namespace already exists (given name), the name is taken on the cluster (UNIQUE_INSTANCE_NAMES), no free generated name, the per-user instance limit of the cluster is reached, or the cluster of the source instance no longer exists ({error})

post.description: Trigger Helm deployment for a stack instance. Allowed for draft, stopped, error, partial and running instances (running = redeploy, a Helm upgrade with the current values). With a TTL, the expiry becomes now + ttl_minutes, unless the current expiry is later (a redeploy never makes the expiry earlier). A fixed stop time (ttl_minutes 0 with expires_at) stays; when it has passed, the deploy gives 409 "The stop time has passed. Set a new stop time or a TTL."

403.description: Caller is not the owner, an admin or a devops user

409.description: Already deploying, or the fixed stop time has passed

get.description:
Get deployment log history for a stack instance, newest first. Supports cursor-based pagination for efficient large dataset traversal.
The default view (full) returns all fields of each log. The summary view returns the row columns only (no output, values_snapshot or chart_versions) and, without a cursor, highlights (running log, current deploy, latest failure; computed over all logs of the instance, the filters do not apply).
The offset path returns total and, when more rows follow, next_cursor. The cursor path returns total: -1.
When the highlights cannot be read, the response has no highlights (the list is still returned).

parameters.description: Page size (default 50, maximum 100; a larger value gives 100)

Returns the merged Helm values that were used for a specific deployment

get.description: Compare pending merged values against the running values per chart. Pending values use the deploy pipeline: cluster shared values (by priority), chart defaults, instance overrides, locked template values. Previous values are the values of the last deploy, or of the last successful rollback. has_changes compares the YAML content (key order and formatting do not matter). values_drift is true when the last operation was a successful rollback and at least one chart has changes: the next deploy undoes the rollback. A shared values load error returns 500 (fail closed).

post.description:
Extend the expiry time of a stack instance. The extend never makes the expiry earlier and never changes ttl_minutes.
- {"minutes": N}: adds N minutes (N > 0) to the current expires_at, or to now when the instance already expired or has no expiry time. The new expiry is capped at now + MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS (default 30 days).
- {"until": "<RFC 3339>"}: sets expires_at to this time. It must be after the current expiry (or after now when the expiry has passed) and not later than now + MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS (400). It works for a TTL and for a fixed stop time. Do not send it with minutes or ttl_minutes (400).
- Empty body: adds the instance's ttl_minutes in the same way (400 when ttl_minutes is 0).
- Deprecated {"ttl_minutes": N} (without minutes): the old behaviour for older clients (stackctl 0.4.0 and earlier). It sets ttl_minutes to N and expires_at to now + N, which can make the expiry earlier. The response has a Warning header; the server logs a deprecation warning.
An instance without TTL and without expiry time has nothing to extend (400).

parameters.description: Minutes to add, the new expiry (until), or the deprecated ttl_minutes
parameters.name: body

200.description: The instance with the new expires_at and the same computed fields as GET (values_drift, names, follow state)

Warning.description: Set when the deprecated ttl_minutes body is used

post.description: The caller follows the instance and gets its in-app notifications, as the owner does, filtered by the notification preferences of the caller. Every authenticated user who can view the instance can follow it. A repeated follow is not an error. Followers get no channel (webhook) deliveries.

delete.description: The caller stops following the instance. Unfollowing an instance that the caller does not follow is not an error.

Returns the quota that applies to the namespace of the instance: the cluster quota of the instance's cluster (the default cluster when the instance has none) merged with the instance quota override, with the same merge as the deployer. A non-empty override quantity replaces the cluster value, and an override pod_limit (also 0) replaces the cluster pod_limit. sources names the origin of each field of effective: override, cluster or none. In effective, an empty quantity means no value and pod_limit 0 means no limit. cluster and override are null when they are not set; cluster_id is empty when the instance has no cluster and no default cluster exists. valid is false when the merged quota breaks a quota rule (models.ValidateEffectiveQuota, the check of the deployer and of the background quota write); invalid_reason then names the field, the values and their source, and a deploy of the instance fails until the quota is fixed. can_modify is true when the caller may set or delete the override (the owner, admin or devops). Any authenticated user can read it.
get.summary: Get the effective quota of an instance

get.description: Retrieve the per-instance resource quota override for a stack instance
get.summary: Get quota override for an instance

put.description:
PUT replaces all fields of the override: a field that is not sent is cleared (an empty quantity or a missing pod_limit means no override for that field, so the cluster quota applies). To change one field, read the override with GET, change the field and send all fields. There is no PATCH.
Upsert the per-instance resource quota override for a stack instance. Each non-empty quantity must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (for example 500m, 2, 512Mi, 10Gi) and not negative; cpu_request must not exceed cpu_limit and memory_request must not exceed memory_limit; pod_limit must not be negative. The container_* fields (LimitRange defaultRequest, default and max per container) and ephemeral_storage_limit follow the same per-field merge: a non-empty value replaces the cluster value. Per container, request <= limit <= max, and a container default must not exceed the namespace value of the same resource. Values are trimmed. The effective quota (cluster quota of the instance's cluster merged with this override) must follow the same rules, for example "cpu_request 4 (instance override) exceeds the effective cpu_limit 2 (cluster quota)". Invalid input returns 400 with the field name. Authorization: the instance owner, admin or devops. An owner without the admin or devops role cannot set a value above the cluster quota of the instance's cluster (403, for example "cpu_limit 64 exceeds the cluster quota 16; only admin or devops can set a higher quota"); the check covers every field, also the container_* fields and ephemeral_storage_limit; a field without a cluster value has no cap, and pod_limit 0 (no limit) counts as above a cluster pod_limit. A value equal to the stored override passes, so an owner can change one field without losing an admin grant. Admin and devops may exceed the cluster quota. The check runs on write (and on clone), not on deploy. After the write, the backend applies the effective quota to the namespace of a deployed instance in the background (not for a draft or cleaning instance). The backend logs a failure, and the next deploy applies the quota.
put.summary: Set or update quota override for an instance

delete.description: Remove the per-instance resource quota override for a stack instance. The backend then applies the cluster quota to the namespace of a deployed instance in the background (not for a draft or cleaning instance). Without a cluster quota, the namespace keeps its current ResourceQuota and LimitRange until the instance is cleaned.
delete.summary: Delete quota override for an instance

post.description:
Without target_log_id: roll back every Helm release of the instance by one revision (helm rollback).
With target_log_id: restore the values of that deploy. The log must be a successful deploy of this instance with a values snapshot (404 when the log does not exist or belongs to another instance, 400 otherwise). Each chart of the target deploy is upgraded (helm upgrade --install) with the merged values of that deploy and the chart version that the deploy recorded; deploys from before the version recording use the current chart version. Charts that the target deploy did not include are left unchanged.
A rollback to a target restores the stored VALUES of that deploy (including the shared and locked values of that time), not the images. Image tags that are branch names can point to newer images now. A chart without a recorded version (the deploy used an empty chart version) installs the newest chart. Pre-deploy hooks do not run for a rollback; subscribe image gates to pre-rollback, which gets the same chart list (name, version, branch, image_tag) plus metadata rollback_mode, target_log_id and target_branch.
The pre-rollback hook runs in the background after the 202 answer, with progress streaming like pre-deploy. A rejection ends the rollback log with status error and the hook reason; the instance gets its previous status back. For a one-revision rollback the hook chart branches come from the previous successful deploy log when it recorded a branch.
In both modes a release stuck in pending-* is cleared before each chart, and after the rollback the instance waits for pod readiness (stabilizing) when readiness gating is configured, as for a deploy. A one-revision rollback that fails records the values of the charts that it already rolled back.
The rollback does not change the stored value or branch overrides. After a successful rollback the deploy preview compares against the running values; values_drift (in this response for a target, and in the deploy preview) shows that the next deploy applies the stored overrides again.

400.description: Invalid body, no charts, or the target is not a successful deploy with a values snapshot

403.description: Caller is not the owner, an admin or a devops user

404.description: Instance or target deploy log not found

get.description:
List published templates for regular users, all templates for devops/admin. Includes definition_count and owner_username (omitted when the owner no longer exists). Supports server-side pagination.
name filters by exact template name (same as the stack-definitions name filter); the response keeps the paged envelope.

200.description: Paginated list with data, total, page, pageSize

post.description:
Create a new stack template (devops/admin only). May include a `charts` array to register the initial chart set in the same transaction.
With is_published=true the template is published in the same transaction (first version snapshot; version is then required). A failed publish rolls the create back.
Delete multiple stack templates in a single request. Only unpublished templates with no linked definitions can be deleted.

Publish multiple stack templates in a single request, making them visible to all users. Each template is published as POST /templates/{id}/publish without a body: the working copy version is used, an unchanged template creates no snapshot, and a version that already exists with other content fails for that template.
Unpublish multiple stack templates in a single request, hiding them from regular users.

get.description:
Get a stack template by ID, including its chart configurations. The template fields and charts are the working copy (draft). owner_username is the username of the owner (omitted when the owner no longer exists).
published_version and published_version_id describe the latest published snapshot (null when there is none). has_unpublished_changes is true when the working copy differs from that snapshot (or there is no snapshot).
published_charts are the charts of that snapshot (what Use Template and Quick Deploy apply; null when there is none). Their IDs are valid chart_overrides keys for Use Template.
charts are the working copy charts only for the template owner and admins. For other users charts equals published_charts (an empty list without a snapshot), version is the published version (empty without a snapshot) and has_unpublished_changes is false, so draft information is not exposed.

put.description:
Update the working copy (draft) of a stack template (template owner or admin). Allowed while the template is published: users keep getting the latest published snapshot until the next publish.
Partial update: only the fields in the body change. version is trimmed.

delete.description: Delete a stack template if no definitions link to it (template owner or admin)

post.description: Add a new chart configuration to the working copy (draft) of a stack template. Users get the change after the next publish. Template owner or admin only.
post.summary: Add a chart to a template

delete.description: Remove a chart configuration from the working copy (draft) of a stack template. Users get the change after the next publish. Template owner or admin only.

post.description:
Create a new draft template that is a copy of the source (devops/admin only).
The body is optional. name sets the name of the clone (trimmed, same rules as create); the default is "<source name> (Copy)".

Create a StackDefinition and ChartConfigs from the latest published snapshot of a template (not the working copy). Definition names are unique per owner.
A template that is not published, or has no snapshot, gives 409 "Template has no published version".
chart_overrides replace chart default values; keys are published_charts[].id, working copy charts[].id (mapped by chart name) or chart names. Keys for charts not in the published snapshot are ignored.

parameters.description: Definition name, description and optional chart_overrides (default values per chart)
parameters.name: body

409.description: The caller already has a definition with this name, or the template has no published version

post.description:
Store the working copy (template fields + charts) as a new version snapshot and make the template visible to all users (template owner or admin).
The body is optional. version (trimmed) defaults to the version of the working copy; the working copy takes the published version.
A version that already exists for the template gives 409 "Version x already exists".
When the working copy equals the latest snapshot (same content and version), no snapshot is created (snapshot_created=false) and the response is 200: publish is idempotent.
Use Template, Quick Deploy and definition upgrades read the latest snapshot, never the working copy.

Instantiate a template, create an instance, set branch overrides, and trigger deployment in a single call.
instance_name must be a DNS label (lowercase a-z, 0-9, '-', start and end alphanumeric, at most 50 characters).
Expiry: ttl_minutes (omitted: DEFAULT_INSTANCE_TTL_MINUTES; 0: no expiry) or expires_at, a fixed stop time (RFC 3339 with a time zone, in the future, not later than now + MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS). Do not send both (400).
The template content comes from the latest published snapshot, not the working copy. A template that is not published, or has no snapshot, gives 409 "Template has no published version".
The new stack definition is owned by the instance (owner_instance_id): deleting the instance deletes the definition when no other instance uses it. The definition is named after the instance; when the caller already has a definition with that name, the name gets the suffix " (2)", " (3)", ...
The owner and the subscribed notification channels get the notification instance.created, with the caller as the trigger.

409.description: Namespace already exists, the name is taken on the cluster (UNIQUE_INSTANCE_NAMES), the template has no published version, or the per-user instance limit of the cluster is reached ({error})

post.description: Hide a template from regular users (template owner or admin). Use Template and Quick Deploy return 409 until the next publish. The version history stays.

get.description: List all version snapshots for a template, ordered newest first. The first entry is the published version that users get. created_by_username is the author's username (omitted when unknown).

Compare two template version snapshots side by side. Either side may be "working" to compare the working copy (draft), for example left=<latest version ID>&right=working shows the unpublished changes.
Only the template owner and admins can compare the working copy (others get 403).
left.version and right.version are version strings; the other side fields (id, created_by, created_by_username, created_at, is_working_copy) describe the side.
template_diffs lists the changed template fields (name, description, category, default_branch, version) with the left and right value; chart_diffs compares the charts.
Get a specific template version with its parsed snapshot and created_by_username

Returns the display values of the web UI: product title, logo URL and favicon URL (APP_TITLE, APP_LOGO_URL, APP_FAVICON_URL), the start value of the TTL field in the create forms (default_instance_ttl_minutes, DEFAULT_INSTANCE_TTL_MINUTES; 0 means no expiry), and the maximum TTL and stop-time distance in days (max_instance_ttl_days, MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS). Public: no authentication, so the login page can use it. An empty logo_url means the built-in logo. A URL is a same-origin path or an https URL. Cached for 5 minutes.
Returns all registered users. Admin only. PasswordHash is never included.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a user account. Admin only. Cannot delete own account (400). The last enabled admin cannot be deleted (409). The caller must still be an enabled admin in the database (403). Revokes the user's current access tokens and all refresh tokens, and deletes all API keys of the user.

get.description: Returns all API keys for the given user. Admin or own user only.
get.summary: List API keys for a user

post.description: Generates a new API key. An expiration is required: set expires_at (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339) or expires_in_days (positive int), but not both. If API_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS is configured, the expiry must not exceed the limit. The raw key is returned once in raw_key and cannot be retrieved again.
post.summary: Create an API key for a user

delete.description: Deletes the specified API key. Admin or own user only. Open WebSocket connections opened with the key close with code 1008.

put.description: Disables a user account. Admin only. The last enabled admin cannot be disabled (409). The caller must still be an enabled admin in the database (403). Revokes the user's current access tokens and all refresh tokens. API keys stop working while the user is disabled and work again after enable.
Re-enables a previously disabled user account. Admin only. Access tokens issued before the enable stay revoked; the user must log in again.
Resets the password for a local/service account user. Admin only. Revokes the user's current access tokens and all refresh tokens. API keys stay valid.

Sets the role of a local user. Admin only. The role of an SSO user comes from the identity provider and cannot be changed here (409). An admin cannot change their own role (403), the caller must still be an enabled admin in the database (403), and the last enabled admin cannot lose the admin role (the own-role and enabled-admin checks reach this first; the 409 is defense in depth). An unchanged role is a no-op (changed=false) and writes no audit entry. A change revokes the user's current access tokens, all refresh tokens and open WebSocket connections, so the next request needs a new login with the new role. API keys stay valid and use the new role at once.
put.summary: Change the role of a user

get.description: Get API health status
Get API liveness status
Get API readiness status

Upgrades the HTTP connection to a WebSocket for real-time events. Authenticate via one of: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: bearer, <jwt>` subprotocol header, `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header, `X-API-Key: sk_<key>` header, or `?token=<jwt>` query parameter (the query token is redacted from access logs and traces by middleware before the handler runs). An API key is accepted only in the X-API-Key header, never in the query. The upgrade runs the same checks as the HTTP auth: a revoked token (logout), a token issued at or before a user block (user deleted, disabled or password reset), an unknown, deleted or expired API key, a deleted user and a disabled user get 401. An API-key upgrade counts against the per-IP API rate limit before the key lookup (429), and gets 503 when the server has no free slot for an Argon2id key verify. The server closes an open socket with close code 1008 when the session or the API key is revoked (key deleted; user deleted, disabled, password reset or role change, which also close the API-key sockets of the user although HTTP API-key requests keep working), when the access token expires and when the API key expires; the client must reconnect.

parameters.description: JWT authentication token (also accepted via Authorization header or Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol)
parameters.name: token

parameters.description: API key (sk_<key>); header only, used when no JWT is sent in the subprotocol or the Authorization header
parameters.name: X-API-Key

origin.description:
Origin is the API origin of the provider (scheme, host and optional
port). It is set only for GitLab, whose origin is configurable
(GITLAB_BASE_URL), so that clients can attribute repository URLs the
same way as the registry. It never contains credentials or a path.

role.description: Role is the new role: "user", "devops" or "admin".

changed.description:
Changed is false when the user already had the role (no-op: the
sessions of the user stay valid).

cleaned_at.description:
CleanedAt is the time the last successful clean finished. It is nil
when the instance was not cleaned since its last deploy. A deploy
clears it. Cleanup policies use it for the cleaned_days condition (a
clean also clears LastDeployedAt, so idle_days cannot count from it).

cluster_name.description:
ClusterName is the name of the target cluster. Omitted when the
cluster no longer exists or cluster_id is empty (older instances).

definition_name.description:
DefinitionName is the name of the stack definition. Omitted when the
definition no longer exists.

following.description:
Following and FollowerCount are computed, not stored. GET, PUT and
POST .../extend on /stack-instances/{id} set them: following is true
when the caller follows the instance, follower_count is the number of
followers. List responses do not set them.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. Omitted when the owner
no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

stopped_at.description:
StoppedAt is the time the last successful stop finished. It is nil
when the instance is not stopped. A deploy or a clean clears it.
Cleanup policies use it for the stopped_days condition.

values_drift.description:
ValuesDrift is computed, not stored. GET, PUT and POST .../extend on
/stack-instances/{id} set it to true when the running values come from
a successful rollback and the stored overrides produce different values
(the next deploy undoes the rollback). List responses do not compute it.

warning.description:
Warning is set when the clone did not get the quota override of the
source (above the cluster quota, or the cluster quota lookup failed).
The clone then uses the cluster quota.

source_template.description:
SourceTemplate is the template that the definition is linked to. The
export sets it for a linked definition; the import links the new
definition when the template and the version exist.

chart_count.description:
ChartCount is the number of charts. It is computed, not stored; the
paged list sets it (the list does not load the charts).

owner_instance_id.description:
OwnerInstanceID is set when quick deploy created the definition for one
instance. Deleting that instance also deletes the definition when no
other instance uses it. Empty for definitions that users create.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. It is computed, not
stored; the API sets it in list and detail responses. Omitted when
the owner no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

values_drift.description:
ValuesDrift is true when the running values come from a rollback (the
last operation was a successful rollback) and the stored overrides
produce different values: the next deploy undoes the rollback.

warning.description: Warning explains ValuesDrift when it is true.

invalid_reason.description: InvalidReason is the validation error of the merged quota (empty when valid).
invalid_reason.example: cpu_request 3 (instance override) exceeds the effective cpu_limit 2 (cluster quota)

sources.description: Sources maps each field of effective to "override", "cluster" or "none".

valid.description: Valid is false when the merged quota breaks a quota rule; a deploy then fails.

helm_releases.description: HelmReleases is always an array, never null.

managed.description:
Managed is true when the namespace has the label
managed-by=k8s-stack-manager. An unmanaged namespace can belong to
another team or tool; deleting it requires ?confirm=<namespace>.

deploy_log_retention_days.description:
DeployLogRetentionDays is DEPLOY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS. The deploy counts
(here, per template and per user) cover only the kept deploy logs:
about the last N days. 0 means all deploy logs are kept.

target_log_id.description:
TargetLogID is the deploy whose values the rollback restores. Empty
for a rollback by one Helm revision.

values_drift.description:
ValuesDrift is set for a rollback to a target: true when the values
built from the stored overrides differ from the target values. The
rollback does not change the stored overrides, so the next deploy then
changes the running values again. Not set for a rollback by one
revision; use GET /deploy-preview after the rollback.

warning.description: Warning explains ValuesDrift when it is true.

version.description:
Version is a published version of the template. Empty means the
latest published version.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. It is computed, not
stored; the API sets it in list and detail responses. Omitted when
the owner no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

published_charts.description:
PublishedCharts are the charts of the latest snapshot: what Use
Template and Quick Deploy apply. The IDs are the template chart config
IDs at publish time; Use Template accepts them as chart_overrides keys.
Null when the template has no snapshot.

default_instance_ttl_minutes.description:
DefaultInstanceTTLMinutes is the start value of the TTL field in the
create forms (DEFAULT_INSTANCE_TTL_MINUTES). 0: no expiry.

favicon_url.description: FaviconURL is the browser tab icon (APP_FAVICON_URL).

logo_url.description: LogoURL is the logo image (APP_LOGO_URL). Empty: the built-in logo.

max_instance_ttl_days.description:
MaxInstanceTTLDays is the maximum TTL and the maximum distance of a
stop time from now (MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS). The forms limit the
TTL field and the stop-time picker with it.

container_cpu_request.description: Per-container LimitRange values and the namespace ephemeral-storage total.

branch.description: Branch is the branch name from the request.

valid.description: Valid is true when the branch exists in the repository.

can_invoke.description: CanInvoke is true when the caller may run the action on this instance.

has_job_log.description:
HasJobLog is true when the backend proxies the job log of the action
(the action config has a log_path).

done.description: Done is true when the job has ended and the log is read to the end.

log.description: Log is the log text from Offset to NextOffset.

next_offset.description: NextOffset is the offset for the next poll.

offset.description: Offset is the requested byte offset.

status.description:
Status is the job state from the subscriber: running while the job
runs, else a final state such as succeeded or failed.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the chunk was cut at the size cap; poll again
at once with next_offset.

scope_incomplete.description:
ScopeIncomplete is true when an action limited to some templates
(applies_to) was left out because the template of the instance could
not be read. Omitted when false.

sensitive.description:
Sensitive is true when the run history stores "[redacted]" instead of
the value; the web UI uses a password field.

action_label.description: ActionLabel is the current label of the action, else its name.

finished_at.description:
FinishedAt is the answer time of a run without a job, or the time the
job log proxy saw the final job status.

has_job_log.description:
HasJobLog is true when the run has a job and the action still has a
log_path.

parameters.description:
Parameters holds the declared parameters only; a sensitive value is
"[redacted]".

started_by.description: StartedBy is the username of user_id; omitted when the user is gone.

status_code.description: StatusCode is the HTTP status of the subscriber; 0 means no answer.

can_view_logs.description:
CanViewLogs is true when the caller may read job logs (owner, admin,
devops).

next_cursor.description: NextCursor loads the next page; omitted on the last page.

left_chart_version.description:
Chart source fields; compared only when both sides store them
(snapshot schema version 1 or the working copy).

branch.description: Branch of the clone. Default: the branch of the source.

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is a fixed stop time of the clone (RFC 3339 with a time
zone). Do not send it with ttl_minutes. Default: a future fixed stop
time of the source.

name.description:
Name of the clone. Must be a DNS label (lowercase a-z, 0-9, '-', start
and end alphanumeric, at most 50 characters). When empty, the server
picks the first free name of <source>-copy, <source>-copy-2, ...

ttl_minutes.description: TTLMinutes of the clone (0 = no expiry). Default: the TTL of the source.

name.description: Name of the clone. Default: "<source name> (Copy)".

filters.description:
Filters limits the channel to some stack instances. Omit it or send
empty lists for all instances.

format.description:
Format is the body format: "generic" (the event JSON, default) or
"teams" (a Microsoft Teams Adaptive Card envelope).

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is a fixed stop time (RFC 3339 with a time zone). It sets
ttl_minutes to 0, and a deploy keeps it. Do not send it with ttl_minutes.

chart_count.description:
ChartCount is the number of charts. It is computed, not stored; the
paged list sets it (the list does not load the charts).

owner_instance_id.description:
OwnerInstanceID is set when quick deploy created the definition for one
instance. Deleting that instance also deletes the definition when no
other instance uses it. Empty for definitions that users create.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. It is computed, not
stored; the API sets it in list and detail responses. Omitted when
the owner no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

minutes.description:
Minutes adds this many minutes to the current expiry (or to now when
the instance already expired or has no expiry time). Must be > 0.

ttl_minutes.description:
TTLMinutes is deprecated. Sent alone, it keeps the old behaviour: set
the TTL to this value and the expiry to now + TTL. Use minutes instead.

until.description:
Until sets the expiry to this time (RFC 3339 with a time zone). It must
be after the current expiry and not later than now plus the limit
(MAX_INSTANCE_TTL_DAYS). Do not send it with minutes or ttl_minutes.

follower_count.description: FollowerCount is the number of users who follow the instance.

following.description: Following is true when the caller follows the instance.

chart_overrides.description:
ChartOverrides replace the default values of charts in the new
definition. Key: a published_charts[].id, a working copy charts[].id
(mapped by chart name) or a chart name. Keys for charts that are not in
the published snapshot are ignored.

enabled.description:
Enabled has no GORM default on purpose: with default:true GORM
writes true for a new channel with enabled=false (zero value). The
handler sets true when the request omits it; the column keeps its
database default (migration 40).

filters.description:
Filters limits the events of the channel to some stack instances.
Empty filters (the default) let all events through.

format.description:
Format is the body format of the webhook request:
NotificationChannelFormatGeneric (the event JSON) or
NotificationChannelFormatTeams (a Microsoft Teams Adaptive Card
envelope). Migration 60 adds the column; existing rows get "generic".

secret_unreadable.description:
SecretUnreadable is set by the repository when the stored secret cannot
be decrypted. Secret is then empty, the channel sends nothing, and a
PUT with a new secret repairs the row.

warnings.description:
Warnings lists filter IDs that point to no existing user, stack
definition or cluster. The channel is saved with them.

webhook_url.description: https URL, at most 2048 characters; empty when webhook_url_unreadable.

webhook_url_unreadable.description:
WebhookURLUnreadable is set by the repository when the stored webhook
URL cannot be decrypted. WebhookURL is then empty, the channel sends
nothing, and a PUT with a new URL repairs the row.

change_summary.description: ChangeSummary is stored with the snapshot.

version.description: Version of the new snapshot. Default: the version of the working copy.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. It is computed, not
stored; the API sets it in list and detail responses. Omitted when
the owner no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is a fixed stop time (RFC 3339 with a time zone). It sets
ttl_minutes to 0. Do not send it with ttl_minutes.

target_log_id.description: TargetLogID is the ID of a successful deploy log of this instance.

container_cpu_request.description: Per-container LimitRange values and the namespace ephemeral-storage total.

template_id.description: TemplateID is the template to link. Empty removes the link.

version.description:
Version is a published version of the template. Empty means the
latest published version.

filters.description:
Filters replaces the filters of the channel. Omit it to keep them;
send {} to remove all filters.

format.description:
Format replaces the body format ("generic" or "teams"). Omit it to
keep the format.

reason.description:
Reason says why there is no upgrade (only when upgrade_available is
false): no_source_template, no_published_version or up_to_date.

created_by_username.description: CreatedByUsername is the author's username (omitted when unknown).

requested_cpu.description:
RequestedCPU and RequestedMemory are the sums of the pod requests
(scheduler rule) of all scheduled pods that are not finished. They are
not real use (metrics-server). Only GET /clusters/:id/health/summary
sets them (GetClusterRequests); empty when the pod list fails.

primary.description:
Primary is true for an Ingress with the annotation
PrimaryURLAnnotation = "true". Primary entries come first in
NamespaceStatus.Ingresses, so clients that show one URL show it.

managed.description:
Managed is true when the namespace has the label
managed-by=k8s-stack-manager (set by the deployer).

prefix.description: first 16 chars of raw key for display

entity_id.description: 63: RFC 1123 label (namespace name); a UUID has 36

build_pipeline_id.description: CI pipeline ID to trigger for image builds

dry_run.description: If true, only report matches without acting

registry_url.description:
Registry fields for automatic image pull secret provisioning.
When RegistryURL is non-empty, a docker-registry secret is created/refreshed
in each stack namespace before chart installs.

current.description:
Current is the deploy whose values run now: the newest successful or
partial deploy, or the target of a newer successful rollback. Nil when
that rollback has no target or its target is not a log of the
instance.

latest_failure.description:
LatestFailure is the newest error log that started after the newest
successful or partial deploy or rollback (any error log when there is
none). A partial log is never a failure here.

running.description: Running is the newest running log (any action).

branch.description:
Branch is the instance branch of a deploy, or the branch of the target
deploy for a rollback to a target. Empty for older logs and for stop
and clean logs.

chart_versions.description:
ChartVersions is a JSON object chart name -> chart version that a
deploy used. A rollback to this deploy installs the same versions.
Empty for logs written before the column existed.

started_by.description:
StartedBy is the username of UserID. The deploy log handlers set it
with one batch lookup. Empty when the user is not known.

user_id.description:
UserID is the user who started a deploy. Per-user analytics count
deploys by this field, so the history stays after the instance is
deleted. Empty for system deploys and for other actions. Migration 49
sets it for older deploy logs to the owner of the instance and adds
the composite index idx_deployment_logs_user_action (user_id, action,
started_at, completed_at, status) for SummarizeByUsers.

highlights.description: Highlights is set only in the summary view without a cursor.

container_cpu_request.description:
Per-container values for the namespace LimitRange (stack-manager-limits)
and the namespace ephemeral-storage total. Empty means not set. See
k8s.Client.EnsureLimitRange for the fallback defaults.

instance_name_patterns.description:
InstanceNamePatterns are glob patterns (path.Match syntax: *, ?,
[a-z]) for the instance name, for example "rdbtest-*". The match
ignores case.

owner_ids.description: OwnerIDs are user IDs of instance owners.

total.description:
Total is the number of matching notifications. It is exact unless
total_capped is true; then it is offset + 1000, and at least
total + 1 notifications match.

total_capped.description:
TotalCapped (total_capped) is true when more than offset + 1000
notifications match. total is then offset + 1000, a lower bound: at
least total + 1 notifications exist.

unread_count.description:
UnreadCount is the number of unread notifications of the user. It is
exact unless unread_count_capped is true; then it is 1000, and the
user has at least 1001 unread notifications.

unread_count_capped.description:
UnreadCountCapped (unread_count_capped) is true when the user has more
than 1000 unread notifications. unread_count is then 1000.

container_cpu_request.description:
Per-container values for the namespace LimitRange (stack-manager-limits)
and the namespace ephemeral-storage total. Empty means not set. See
k8s.Client.EnsureLimitRange for the fallback defaults.

chart_count.description:
ChartCount is the number of charts. It is computed, not stored; the
paged list sets it (the list does not load the charts).

OwnerInstanceID is set when quick deploy created the definition for one
instance. Deleting that instance also deletes the definition when no
other instance uses it. Empty for definitions that users create.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. It is computed, not
stored; the API sets it in list and detail responses. Omitted when
the owner no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

cleaned_at.description:
CleanedAt is the time the last successful clean finished. It is nil
when the instance was not cleaned since its last deploy. A deploy
clears it. Cleanup policies use it for the cleaned_days condition (a
clean also clears LastDeployedAt, so idle_days cannot count from it).

cluster_name.description:
ClusterName is the name of the target cluster. Omitted when the
cluster no longer exists or cluster_id is empty (older instances).

definition_name.description:
DefinitionName is the name of the stack definition. Omitted when the
definition no longer exists.

following.description:
Following and FollowerCount are computed, not stored. GET, PUT and
POST .../extend on /stack-instances/{id} set them: following is true
when the caller follows the instance, follower_count is the number of
followers. List responses do not set them.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. Omitted when the owner
no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

stopped_at.description:
StoppedAt is the time the last successful stop finished. It is nil
when the instance is not stopped. A deploy or a clean clears it.
Cleanup policies use it for the stopped_days condition.

values_drift.description:
ValuesDrift is computed, not stored. GET, PUT and POST .../extend on
/stack-instances/{id} set it to true when the running values come from
a successful rollback and the stored overrides produce different values
(the next deploy undoes the rollback). List responses do not compute it.

owner_username.description:
OwnerUsername is the username of the owner. It is computed, not
stored; the API sets it in list and detail responses. Omitted when
the owner no longer exists (for example, after a delete).

build_pipeline_id.description: CI pipeline ID to trigger for image builds

id.description:
Fields below exist from schema version 1.
ID is the template chart config ID in the working copy at publish time.
It is not content: SameTemplateContent ignores it.

user has at least 1001 unread notifications.

UnreadCountCapped (unread_count_capped) is true when the user has more
than 1000 unread notifications.
